items.text: Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the Lord your God gives you.
items.quote: Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the Lord your God gives you.

items.text: Obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.
items.quote: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.

items.text: Show honor, affection, and gratitude toward elders and ancestors.
items.quote: It requires honor, affection, and gratitude toward elders and ancestors.

heading: IV. The Family and the Kingdom · 2232 … 2233

items.text: Respect the vocation God gives your child and encourage him to follow it.
items.quote: Parents should respect this call and encourage their children to follow it.

items.text: Welcome with joy and thanksgiving the Lord's call to your child to follow him in virginity for the Kingdom in the consecrated life or priestly ministry.
items.quote: Parents should welcome and respect with joy and thanksgiving the Lord's call to one of their children to follow him in virginity for the sake of the Kingdom
items.conflict: Vows of celibacy and a separate priesthood (1 Tim 4:1-3; Heb 10:11-14)

work: "Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§ 2196–2257: The Fourth Commandment"
heading: III. The Duties of Family Members · 2228 … 2231

items.text: Bring up your young children and provide for their physical and spiritual needs; as they grow, educate them in the right use of their reason and freedom.
items.quote: care and attention they devote to bringing up their young children and providing for their physical and spiritual needs

items.text: Choose for your children a school that corresponds to your own convictions and best helps you as Christian educators.
items.quote: parents have the duty of choosing schools that will best help them in their task as Christian educators.

items.text: Assume your new responsibilities within a trusting relationship with your parents; willingly ask and receive their advice and counsel.
items.quote: They should assume their new responsibilities within a trusting relationship with their parents, willingly asking and receiving their advice and counsel.

items.text: Do not exert pressure on your children in their choice of a profession or spouse; give them judicious advice, especially when they plan to start a family.
items.quote: Parents should be careful not to exert pressure on their children either in the choice of a profession or in that of a spouse.

work: "Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§ 2196–2257: The Fourth Commandment"
heading: I. The Family in God's Plan · 2201 · The nature of the family … 2206

items.text: Love one another and order your common life to the good of your spouse.
items.quote: The love of the spouses and the begetting of children create among members of the same family personal relationships and primordial responsibilities.

items.text: Welcome procreation and educate your children, ordering the family to their upbringing.
items.quote: Marriage and the family are ordered to the good of the spouses and to the procreation and education of children.

items.text: Respect one another as family members equal in dignity.
items.quote: The relationships within the family bring an affinity of feelings, affections and interests, arising above all from the members' respect for one another.

items.text: Take part in daily prayer and the reading of the Word of God within the family.
items.quote: Daily prayer and the reading of the Word of God strengthen it in charity.

items.text: Deliberate together and share your thought as spouses.
items.quote: A sharing of thought and common deliberation by the spouses as well as their eager cooperation as parents in the children's upbringing.

items.text: Cooperate eagerly as parents in the upbringing of your children.
items.quote: Their eager cooperation as parents in the children's upbringing.

work: "Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§ 2196–2257: The Fourth Commandment"
heading: IN BRIEF · 2247 … 2257

items.text: Honor your father and mother: give them respect, gratitude, just obedience, and assistance.
items.quote: Children owe their parents respect, gratitude, just obedience, and assistance.

items.text: Educate your children in the faith, prayer, and all the virtues.
items.quote: Parents have the first responsibility for the education of their children in the faith, prayer, and all the virtues.

items.text: Provide as far as possible for the physical and spiritual needs of your children.
items.quote: They have the duty to provide as far as possible for the physical and spiritual needs of their children.

items.text: Respect and encourage your children's vocations; remember and teach that the first calling of the Christian is to follow Jesus.
items.quote: Parents should respect and encourage their children's vocations. They should remember and teach that the first calling of the Christian is to follow Jesus.

items.text: Build your marriage upon covenant and consent, and order it to the good of your spouse, the procreation and education of children.
items.quote: Marriage and family are ordered to the good of the spouses, to the procreation and the education of children.

work: "Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§ 2196–2257: The Fourth Commandment"
heading: III. The Duties of Family Members · 2214 · The duties of children … 2227

items.text: Honor your father with all your heart, and do not forget the birth pangs of your mother.
items.quote: With all your heart honor your father, and do not forget the birth pangs of your mother.

items.text: While you live at home, obey your parents in all that they ask of you when it is for your good or that of the family.
items.quote: Children, obey your parents in everything, for this pleases the Lord.

items.text: In old age and in times of illness, loneliness, or distress, give your parents material and moral support as much as you can.
items.quote: As much as they can, they must give them material and moral support in old age and in times of illness, loneliness, or distress.

items.text: Support one another in charity with all humility, meekness, and patience.
items.quote: With all humility and meekness, with patience, support one another in charity.

items.text: Show special gratitude to your parents and grandparents for handing on to you the gift of faith, Baptism, and life in the Church.
items.quote: For Christians a special gratitude is due to those from whom they have received the gift of faith, the grace of Baptism, and life in the Church.

items.text: Educate your children morally and spiritually; this right and duty is primordial and inalienable.
items.quote: The right and the duty of parents to educate their children are primordial and inalienable.

items.text: Bring up your children in the discipline and instruction of the Lord, and give them good example.
items.quote: Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.

items.text: Teach your children to avoid the compromising and degrading influences that threaten human societies.
items.quote: Parents should teach children to avoid the compromising and degrading influences which threaten human societies.

items.text: Initiate your children at an early age into the mysteries of the faith, and associate them with the life of the Church.
items.quote: Parents should initiate their children at an early age into the mysteries of the faith of which they are the first heralds for their children.

items.text: Teach your children to pray and to discover their vocation as children of God.
items.quote: Parents have the mission of teaching their children to pray and to discover their vocation as children of God.

items.text: Contribute to the growth in holiness of your parents.
items.quote: Children in turn contribute to the growth in holiness of their parents.

items.text: Forgive one another generously and tirelessly for offenses, quarrels, injustices, and neglect.
items.quote: Each and everyone should be generous and tireless in forgiving one another for offenses, quarrels, injustices, and neglect.

work: "Catechism of the Catholic Church, §§ 2196–2257: The Fourth Commandment"
heading: II. The Family and Society · 2207 … 2213

items.text: Give yourselves to each other in love and in the gift of life.
items.quote: husband and wife are called to give themselves in love and in the gift of life

items.text: Train the children of your household from childhood to learn moral values, honor God, and make good use of freedom.
items.quote: the family is the community in which, from childhood, one can learn moral values, begin to honor God, and make good use of freedom

items.text: Take responsibility for the young, the old, the sick, the handicapped, and the poor in your family.
items.quote: The family should live in such a way that its members learn to care and take responsibility for the young, the old, the sick, the handicapped, and the poor.

items.text: Visit widows in their affliction and keep yourself unstained from the world.
items.quote: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction and to keep oneself unstained from the world

items.text: Visit orphans in their affliction and keep yourself unstained from the world.
items.quote: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction and to keep oneself unstained from the world

items.text: See in your brothers and sisters the children of your parents, and give them particular attention and respect.
items.quote: In our brothers and sisters we see the children of our parents

items.text: See in your cousins the descendants of your ancestors, and give them particular attention and respect.
items.quote: in our cousins, the descendants of our ancestors
